title: Śrī Śrī Upadeśāmṛta
author: by Śrīla Rūpa Goswāmī Prabhu in Sanskrit
subtitle: Verse Six

translation: Being situated in one’s original Kṛṣṇa conscious position, a pure devo­tee does not identify with the body. Such a devotee should not be seen from a materialistic point of view. Indeed, one should overlook a devotee’s having a body born in a low family, a body with a bad complexion, a deformed body, or a diseased or infirm body. According to ordinary vision, such imperfections may seem prominent in the body of a pure devotee, but despite such seeming defects, the body of a pure devotee cannot be polluted. It is exactly like the waters of the Ganges, which sometimes during the rainy season are full of bubbles, foam, and mud. The Ganges waters do not become polluted. Those who are advanced in spiritual understanding will bathe in the Ganges without considering the condition of the water.
*Śrīla Bhakti Vinod Ṭhākur’s corresponding Bengali composition:*
Ganges water does not lose its spiritual nature because it contains foam, mud, and so on, which are natural in water.
Similarly, pure devotees are not mundane because of faults within their nature and form that are natural in the material body.

text: prākṛta baliyā bhakte kabhu nā nindibe
translation: Therefore, upon seeing the faults produced by a devotee’s nature or occupation, such as ugliness or apparent roughness, never consider a devotee mundane and criticise them. Rather, see their pure bhakti and always revere them.
